Hi Ana — thanks for the clear note and the redline. We reviewed internally (legal + privacy + platform) and prepared a short consolidated exhibit that preserves your intent but clarifies two operational points:

- Subprocessor notice period: your draft requested 30 days. Our standard for reserved/managed subprocessors is 45 days to allow for capacity and contract alignment, but we are open to a hybrid approach (see below).
- Emergency mitigation: we added language for an accelerated notification and mitigation path for high-risk subprocessors (48-hour acknowledgement + 7-day remediation plan).

I've attached Redwood's redline (redwood_response_redline.pdf) and a consolidated exhibit draft (redwood_consolidated_exhibit_v3.docx). To keep this lightweight we propose re-executing via DocuSign so it can be appended to the master DPA without replacing the whole agreement.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick confirm on the subprocessor notice cadence (45 days vs. your preferred 30).
2) If you agree, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and list signers on Redwood's side (Chief Privacy Officer + Head of Contracts).
3) We will include a short amendment cover page referencing the original DPA effective date and the supplemental exhibit identifier.

Timeline: if we get your confirmation by Monday (Nov 1) we can have the envelope ready the same day and aim to complete signatures by Nov 5, meeting your launch window. DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/ABC123-789

Who will sign for Sano? Please confirm the legal and procurement signers and whether DocuSign signature is acceptable.

Thanks — looping in Marissa and Hannah for visibility.

— Logan Wright
Director, Contracts & GTM Legal
Redwood Inference

Logan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the consolidated draft. A few quick points from Sano Legal:

- We prefer to keep the standard subprocessor notice period at 30 days. Our risk team is comfortable with Redwood's emergency mitigation language, but we need the standard notice to remain 30 days.
- If Redwood absolutely requires 45 days for operational reasons, we can accept 45 days for non-critical subprocessors but insist on the 30-day default for any changes that involve data residency or new EU-US transfer paths.
- Procurement (on copy) asks that any administrative fee or pricing change resulting from the new transfer lane be communicated before signature.

Suggested trade: we sign the consolidated exhibit with 30-day notice and include Redwood's 48-hour emergency acknowledgement carve-out for high-risk subprocessors. That keeps our control plane tight while preserving Redwood's operational runway.

Signers for Sano: Ana Rodrigues (Legal) and Jorge M. (VP Procurement) — procurement will handle the DocuSign flow on our end. DocuSign is fine for us. I attached a lightly annotated redline (sano_supplemental_redline_v1.pdf) with the above notes.

If that compromise works, please push the envelope and let me know when it's live.

Thanks,
Ana
